primary_cause: Feb 18 warned would miss March-quarter revenue guidance. Feb 26 Reuters: Foxconn only ~50% Chinese production by end-Feb
secondary_factors: Broader derating of hardware names exposed to China. Rising fears of global consumer electronics demand weakness
store_description: Apple had explicitly said it would miss the March-quarter revenue range and Reuters then reported Foxconn's core iPhone plants were still ramping slowly with only about 50% of Chinese production expected back by end-February. That made Apple a direct COVID casualty not just a passive victim of the tape.

primary_cause: Semiconductor sector derating tied to COVID demand and supply-chain fears
secondary_factors: Investors extrapolating Apple/Foxconn and China manufacturing problems across chip suppliers. General tech multiple compression
store_description: No Broadcom-specific negative headline found. Investors sold AVGO as a high-beta semiconductor name with China and handset exposure while the market was repricing tech supply chains and end demand.

primary_cause: Collapse in crude prices from COVID demand destruction fears. Brent $52.18 WTI $47.09 lowest in 13 months
secondary_factors: Broad risk-off selling in cyclical and energy equities
store_description: No stock-specific ConocoPhillips news found. The move looks overwhelmingly oil-driven. As coronavirus cases outside China accelerated traders repriced global fuel demand lower pushing Brent to about $52 and WTI to about $47.

primary_cause: Broad de-rating of consulting and IT services on fear clients would delay projects
secondary_factors: Macro recession fears. Later cut FY2020 revenue growth to 3-6% from 6-8% on March 19
store_description: No issuer-specific headline in the 3-day lookback. ACN sold off as investors anticipated slower consulting bookings and project delays. Concern later proved valid when the company cut its growth outlook.

primary_cause: No negative stock-specific catalyst. Drop was market-led despite strong Feb 25 earnings
secondary_factors: Investors taking risk off in high-multiple cloud/software despite solid earnings
store_description: Salesforce had just posted $4.85B quarterly revenue (+35% YoY) and raised FY21 revenue guidance to $21.0-21.1B. The Feb 27 decline looks like a valuation compression move in software rather than a reaction to bad company news.

primary_cause: Industrial and aerospace cyclical selloff on fears of weaker air travel production and capex
secondary_factors: Broad risk-off sentiment. Later reaffirmed Q1 and full-year 2020 outlook on March 10
store_description: No direct Honeywell trigger found. Stock most likely fell because investors were rapidly repricing aerospace and industrial demand lower as IATA warned 2020 air travel demand would fall 4.7%.

primary_cause: Broad consumer/cyclical risk-off overwhelmed strong Feb 25 earnings. EPS $2.28 vs $2.10 expected
secondary_factors: Fear that COVID would hit store traffic housing-linked demand and discretionary spending despite good quarter
store_description: Home Depot had delivered a solid print two days earlier beating EPS expectations by $0.18 and raising its dividend 10%. The Feb 27 drop looks more like a macro repricing of consumer-exposed cyclicals than a response to bad HD-specific news.

primary_cause: Bank sector selloff from recession fears and collapsing yields. Goldman itself cut 2020 US earnings growth forecast to zero
secondary_factors: Risk-off hurt capital-markets sensitive names. Weaker trading/IB/credit conditions expected
store_description: No Goldman-specific operational negative found. Stock sold off because investors were pricing in weaker trading investment banking and credit conditions. Goldman itself publicly said U.S. firms would see zero earnings growth in 2020.

primary_cause: Repricing of digital-ad exposure as markets anticipated broad slowdown in advertising
secondary_factors: General mega-cap tech selloff and risk-off across growth stocks
store_description: No distinct Alphabet-specific negative headline found. Investors started discounting weaker ad budgets as COVID spread globally especially from travel and entertainment advertisers while selling liquid mega-cap tech names broadly.

primary_cause: Same as GOOGL. Macro repricing of ad-sensitive mega-cap tech
secondary_factors: Class A and C shares moved together. Driver was macro and business-model related
store_description: GOOG and GOOGL moved together because the driver was macro and business-model related not share-class specific.

primary_cause: Sharp repricing of aviation and industrial exposure amid collapsing travel expectations
secondary_factors: General balance-sheet sensitivity and macro risk-off. GE Aviation later confirmed as most damaged business
store_description: No precise GE corporate event found. Stock likely sold off because GE Aviation was extremely exposed to a rapid deterioration in air travel demand and investors were simultaneously marking down industrial activity.

primary_cause: Industrial/aerospace derating tied to COVID rather than GD-specific announcement
secondary_factors: Gulfstream business-jet demand concerns and broad market deleveraging
store_description: No discrete GD catalyst found. Decline looks consistent with investors marking down aerospace-adjacent names especially those with business-jet exposure through Gulfstream.

primary_cause: Concern that global trade air freight and express volumes would weaken as COVID spread
secondary_factors: Broad industrial/transport selloff. Later suspended 2020 profit outlook March 17
store_description: No FedEx-specific negative release found. FedEx was a very logical macro casualty given its exposure to international commerce and air cargo. Concern later validated when company suspended full-year profit outlook.

primary_cause: Broad industrial capex and manufacturing slowdown fears
secondary_factors: Global factory disruption and commodity-linked weakness
store_description: No distinct Emerson announcement found. Investors sold diversified industrials on expectations that global manufacturing energy and automation spending would weaken.

primary_cause: Company-specific exposure to park travel and film disruption. Shanghai and Hong Kong parks already shut in late January
secondary_factors: Worsening fears around global tourism and entertainment attendance
store_description: Unlike some other names Disney did have a visible company-specific COVID overhang. Shanghai and Hong Kong parks had already been shuttered. Investors were likely extrapolating from those closures to broader theme-park box-office and travel-related pain.

primary_cause: General market liquidation even in defensives
secondary_factors: Concern that lower commercial/industrial power demand and falling rates signaled economic weakness
store_description: No company-specific Duke catalyst found. Utilities held up better than cyclicals but DUK still fell as the selloff became indiscriminate.

primary_cause: Cyclical agriculture/construction machinery demand fears exacerbated by COVID
secondary_factors: Preexisting softness in farm equipment demand. Later withdrew guidance March 23
store_description: No negative Deere headline in the exact Feb 24-27 window but investors already knew the business was late-cycle and exposed to weak equipment demand. COVID added a fresh recession shock.

primary_cause: Oil price collapse from COVID demand fears. Brent $52.18 WTI $47.09 lowest in over a year
secondary_factors: Broad energy equity selloff and recession worries
store_description: No Chevron-specific negative announcement found. Stock's decline best explained by crude's sharp fall to roughly $52 Brent and $47 WTI.

primary_cause: Broad market selloff rather than issuer-specific news
secondary_factors: Healthcare/retail uncertainty. Emerging store-level outbreak pressure with mask/sanitizer shortages
store_description: No solid CVS-specific catalyst found. Stock seems to have been swept down with the tape though the emerging outbreak was already affecting store-level operations and product availability.

primary_cause: Enterprise tech hardware/networking de-rating on concern customers would delay spending
secondary_factors: General tech selloff. Had withdrawn from MWC over coronavirus concerns
store_description: No fresh Cisco-specific negative catalyst found. Investors sold network hardware names on the same logic hitting the broader tech supply chain: China disruption delayed customer purchases and a fast worsening macro outlook.
